expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "Not with just a modal, no. A confirmation dialog sits at rung 2 (warning), but the poka-yoke UX skill shows this is the weakest choice"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "A confirmation dialog a user sees fifty times a day stops being a decision point. They develop click-through blindness and press 'Confirm' with the same reflex they press 'OK'"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: Listed #1: "Make it reversible. Soft-delete with a trash/retention period"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: Listed #2: "Grace-period undo. Delete immediately, show 'Deleted. Undo' toast for 30 seconds"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: "Confirmation dialog naming the exact consequence. 'Delete workspace 'acme-corp' and 3,400 files permanently?'"

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: Clear 1-2-3-4 numbered ranking with specific hierarchy
